KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r1.claim: The account of Moses’ confrontation with Pharaoh and his people supplies historical lessons within the Prophet’s call and struggle for tawhid.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r1.anchor: Buradaki örnek Hz. Mûsâ ile Mısır’ın tanrı kralı Firavun ve tebaası arasında geçen olaylar, tartışmalar ve alınan ibretlik sonuçlardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r2.claim: Unbelievers retain a deep belief in God that worldly incentives and suggestions bury; disasters sent in mercy revive it, but they return to denial when hardship passes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r2.anchor: İnkârcıların bilinçlerinin derinliklerinde bir Allah inancı vardır, çeşitli telkinler ve dünyanın çekici menfaatleri bu temel duyguyu köreltmiş veya üstünü küllerle örtmüştür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r3.claim: Tawhid is every prophet’s shared message: scripture and its remnants show that God never permitted worship of another being, as Moses’ struggle also proves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r3.anchor: Tevhid inancı bütün peygamberlerin ortak tebliğleri ve inanç ilkeleridir. Kendilerine kitap gönderilmiş topluluklara sorulduğunda veya eski kitapların kalıntıları okunduğunda anlaşılmaktadır ki, Allah hiçbir zaman kendisi dışında bir varlığa kulluk edilmesine izin vermemiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r4.claim: The verb istikhfaf can mean hastening, deceiving, exploiting ignorance, belittling people for weakness, or directing them as one wishes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r4.anchor: Bu kelime Arapça’da “acele ettirdi, aldattı, bilgisizliklerinden yararlandı, onları bilgisizlikleri ve güçsüzlükleri yüzünden hafife aldı, istediği gibi yönlendirdi” mânalarını ifade etmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r5.claim: Totalitarian rulers fear an informed, truth-seeking public organized enough to claim its rights; Pharaoh exploited ignorance and spectacle to obstruct Moses, manipulate the people, and preserve his rule.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r5.anchor: Firavun da aynı yola başvurmuş, Hz. Mûsâ’nın gerçeğe ve tevhide yönelik davetini sabote etmiş, halkın sağlıklı düşünmesini engellemiş, geleneklerden ve gözler önündeki alâyişten yararlanarak toplumu âdeta büyülemiş ve saltanatını devam ettirmenin yolunu bulmuştur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r6.speaker: şair
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r6.claim: The author invokes a poet’s line to stress that Pharaoh’s sovereignty has vanished.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r6.claim: Moses and Jesus both called people to monotheism; Pharaoh and his chiefs rejected Moses' successive signs for the same arrogant reason as Quraysh and met their deserved fate, which Quraysh will also face.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r6.anchor: Moses (sws) showed great signs one after the other to the Pharaoh and his chiefs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.claim: Every part of Sūrah al-Zukhruf relates deeply to its central theme, and the whole sūrah forms a harmonious unit from beginning to end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.anchor: each part of it is deeply related to its central theme

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p200/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p200/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p200/r4.claim: The verb istakhafa is opposite to istathqala: Pharaoh treated his people as simpletons, lured them, and they followed foolishly.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p200/r4.anchor: like fools it was entrapped by him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p200/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p200/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p200/r5.claim: Their disobedience and lack of faith left them spiritually insignificant and easy for Satan to lead; a person gains weight through relationship with God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p200/r5.anchor: A person becomes weighty by his relationship with God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p383/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p383/r1.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p383/r1.claim: Ibn al-A'rabi says Pharaoh made his people seem foolish because their understanding was light.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p383/r1.anchor: أي استجهلهم لخفة أحلامهم، قاله ابن الأعرابي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p383/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p383/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p383/r2.claim: Another view says Pharaoh made them pliant and easily led, and their wickedness made them obey him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p383/r2.anchor: حملهم على أن يخفوا لما يريد منهم، فأجابوه لفسقهم

QUSHAYRI:v3p177/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p177/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p177/r10.claim: Pharaoh's people obeyed him from fear, which is not sincere obedience; genuine obedience arises from willingness.
QUSHAYRI:v3p177/r10.anchor: أطاعوه طاعة الرهبة ، وطاعة ’ الرهبة لا تكون مخلصة ، وإنما تكون الطاعة صادقة إذا صدرت عن الرغبة

DURR-FULL:v7p383/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p383/r9.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p383/r9.claim: Ikrimah says Pharaoh did not let out anyone older than forty or younger than twenty, exemplifying how he made his people comply in pursuing Moses.
DURR-FULL:v7p383/r9.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: لم يخرج فرعون من زاد على الأربعين سنة ومن دون العشرين فذلك قوله: {فاستخف قومه فأطاعوه} يعني استخف قومه في طلب موسى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p59/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p59/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p59/r9.claim: Pharaoh made his people pliant to his aim, and they obeyed him in disbelief because of their sinfulness and corruption.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p59/r9.anchor: أي طلب خفتهم وإجابتهم إلى غرضه، فأجابوه إلى ذلك وأطاعوه في الكفر

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r30.speaker: ابن زياد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r30.claim: Ibn Ziyad says Pharaoh stirred his people with speech until they obeyed him in denying Moses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r30.anchor: استفزهم بالقول فأطاعوه على التكذيب ، قاله ابن زياد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r31.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r31.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r31.claim: Al-Farra explains that Pharaoh excited them with inducements, so they readily responded.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r31.anchor: حركهم بالرغبة فخفوا معه في الإجابة ، وهو معنى قول الفراء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r32.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r32.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r32.claim: Al-Kalbi says Pharaoh treated them as ignorant, and their obedience displayed their ignorance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r32.anchor: استجهلهم فأظهروا طاعة جهلهم ، وهو معنى قول الكلبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r33.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r33.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r33.claim: Ibn Isa says Pharaoh called them to falsehood, and they hastened to answer him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p229/r33.anchor: دعاهم إلى باطله فخفوا في إجابته , قاله ابن عيسى .

STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r16.claim: The idolaters’ opposition to the Prophet is likened to Pharaoh and his notables opposing Moses.
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r16.anchor: the opposition of the idolaters to the Prophet is likened to the opposition of Pharaoh and his “notables” toward Moses (vv.46–56)

STUDYQURAN:43:46/r24.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:46/r24.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:46/r24.claim: The phrase about inciting people to make light may instead mean that Pharaoh moved them to submit or to be foolish.
STUDYQURAN:43:46/r24.anchor: Then he incited his people to make light could also mean that he moved them to submit or to be foolish.

TABRISI:43:51-54/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:51-54/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:51-54/r11.claim: Pharaoh made his people’s minds seem foolish, and they obeyed an invalid argument from kingship; property does not prove truth, and messengers need no angels because miracles prove them.
TABRISI:43:51-54/r11.anchor: ومعناه إن فرعون استخف عقول قومه

TABRISI:43:51-54/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:51-54/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:51-54/r12.claim: Pharaoh’s people were outside obedience to God.
TABRISI:43:51-54/r12.anchor: أي خارجين عن طاعة الله تعالى

THALABI:v8p339#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p339#2/r5.speaker: أبو الدرداء
THALABI:v8p339#2/r5.claim: Abu al-Darda says that if the world weighed as little to God as a gnat's wing, Pharaoh would not have been given a drink from it.
THALABI:v8p339#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء: لو كانت الدنيا تزن عند الله جناح ذباب ما سقي فرعون منها شرابا

BURSEVI:v8p291#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p291#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p291#2/r2.claim: Reflecting on Satan and Pharaoh, Bursevi urges purifying the self of the base traits that made them what they became, and asks God for care and guidance before the return to His presence.
BURSEVI:v8p291#2/r2.anchor: فاجتهد في إصلاح النفس وتزكيتها عن الأوصاف الرذيلة التي بها صار الشيطان شيطانا وفرعون فرعونا

BURSEVI:v8p292/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p292/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p292/r3.claim: Pharaoh’s deception made his people intellectually lightweight and quick to obey; the requested lightness concerns their judgment, not bodily speed, or means he found their minds credulous.
BURSEVI:v8p292/r3.anchor: فالمطلوب بما ذكره من التلبيسات والتمويهات خفة عقولهم حتى يطيعوه فيما أراد منهم

BURSEVI:v8p292/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p292/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p292/r4.claim: Al-Raghib allows that Pharaoh made them hasten to follow him or found them lightweight in body and resolve.
BURSEVI:v8p292/r4.anchor: وقال الراغب : حملهم على أن يخفوا معه ،

BURSEVI:v8p292/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p292/r5.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v8p292/r5.claim: Al-Qamus gives استخفه as the opposite of making someone weighty, or as leading someone into ignorance and fickleness and away from sound judgment.
BURSEVI:v8p292/r5.anchor: وفي "القاموس" : استخفه ضد استثقله وفلانا عن رأيه حمله على الجهل والخفة

BURSEVI:v8p292/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p292/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p292/r6.claim: Al-Kashifi says Pharaoh found his group mentally light through this trick, which took effect on them.
BURSEVI:v8p292/r6.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (بس سبك عقل يافت فرعون بدين مكر كروه خودرا يعنى اين فريب در ايشان اثر كرد).

BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r1.claim: They obeyed Pharaoh because they were profoundly ignorant and astray, completely withdrawing from Moses’ way.
BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r1.anchor: {فأطاعوه} فيما أمرهم به لفرط جهلهم وضلالهم.

BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r2.claim: They rushed to obey Pharaoh because they were a wicked people outside God’s obedience and sound reason, trusting transient wealth and rank and looking down on Moses.
BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r2.anchor: {إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين} ، فلذلك سارعوا إلى طاعة ذلك الفاسق الغوي.

BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r3.claim: The commanding self dominates heart, spirit, and their attributes through violation of religious law and surrender to desire; obedience begins in fear and becomes willing as they take on its traits.
BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r3.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" يشير إلى أن كل من استولى على قوم فاستخفهم ، فأطاعوه رهبة منه

BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r4.claim: An enemy never truly submits; do not trust compelled obedience, since, given an opening, the enemy would cut a hand off instead of kissing it.
BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r4.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن العدو لا ينقاد بحال ، وأما انقياده كرها فلا يغتر به ، فإنه لو وجد فرصة لقطع اليد بدل التقبيل

TABATABAI:43:54-56/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:54-56/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:54-56/r1.claim: Pharaoh made his people’s minds and judgment foolish, and so they obeyed him.

TABATABAI:43:54-56/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:54-56/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:54-56/r2.claim: The people are described as transgressors and sinners.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r1.claim: استخفه may mean that joy agitates and unsettles someone, or that someone is made to act ignorantly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r1.anchor: يقال: استخفه الفرح، # إذا أزعجه وأقلقه، واستخفه إذا حمله على الجهل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r2.claim: The related wording in 30:60 means do not let those without certainty drive you into ignorance or incline you toward them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r2.anchor: ومنه قوله: {ولا يستخفنك الذين لا يوقنون} [الروم: 60] أي [لا يحميك] (¬2) على الجهل والميل إليهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r3.claim: Muqatil and al-Farra gloss the verb as provoking the Egyptians; al-Wahidi explains that Pharaoh unsettled them and led them into ignorance through deceit and the claim that he showed them only what he saw.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: فاستفز قومه القبط (¬3)، وهو قول الفراء: استفزهم (¬4)، والمعنى أزعجهم وحملهم على صفة الجهل بكيده وغروره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi rejects interpreting the verb as merely finding the people foolish: their obedience requires Pharaoh to have urged them to something, and that reading needs an impermissible omitted step, unlike the sense of agitating them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r4.anchor: فليس بالوجه لقوله: {فأطاعوه} وهذا يوجب أنه أمرهم بشيء فيه إزعاجهم فأطاعوه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say the people obeyed Pharaoh by rejecting Moses; Pharaoh induced ignorance, and they accepted his claim and denied Moses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: على تكذيب موسى (¬6)، والمعنى أنه حملهم على الجهل فقبلوا قوله وكذبوا موسى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p61/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p61/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p61/r1.claim: The people Moses had led were disobedient to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p61/r1.anchor: إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين} قالا: عاصين لله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:54-57/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:54-57/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:54-57/r1.claim: Pharaoh made his Coptic people out to be ignorant, and they obeyed him; they were a sinful people.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:54-57/r1.anchor: فاستخف قومه } وجد قومه القبط جهالا

FARRA:v3p35/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p35/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p35/r1.claim: Istakh affa qawmahu means he incited and stirred up his people.

NAHHAS:v4p114/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p114/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p114/r1.claim: Pharaoh made his people take his claim lightly and thereby led them to disbelief in Moses.
NAHHAS:v4p114/r1.anchor: أي استخفهم بذلك القول إلى الكفر بموسى صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r1.claim: On the ordinary sense of istikhfāf, Pharaoh sought their eagerness and quickness to comply; khiffa here means speed in answering and following, a familiar metaphor.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r1.anchor: فطلب منهم الخفة في مطاوعته على أن السين للطلب على حقيقتها ومعنى الخفة السرعة لأجابته ومتابعته

ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r2.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r2.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi explains that Pharaoh found their intellects light, meaning deficient; the form denotes finding, as in ahmadtu, and attributing that to the people is figurative.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي استخف أحلامهم أيوجدهم خفيفة أحلامهم أي قليلة عقولهم

ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r3.claim: They obeyed Pharaoh in what he commanded them.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r4.claim: Their own transgression explains why they hurried to obey the transgressing, misguided Pharaoh.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p91/r4.anchor: فلذلك سارعوا إلى طاعة ذلك الفاسق الغوي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217#2/r4.claim: Pharaoh made his Egyptian people seem foolish, finding them ignorant.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217#2/r4.anchor: أي استخف فرعون قومه القبط، أي وجدهم جهالا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217#2/r5.claim: Another gloss is that Pharaoh led them into frivolity and ignorance, removing them from sound judgment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: حملهم على الخفة والجهل. يقال: استخفه عن رأيه، إذا حمله على الجهل وأزاله عن الصواب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217#2/r6.claim: They obeyed Pharaoh by denying Moses, and were a disobedient people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217#2/r6.anchor: على تكذيب موسى، {إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين}

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:54-56/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:54-56/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:54-56/r1.claim: Pharaoh either invited his people to comply readily or made their minds and judgment lightweight.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:54-56/r1.anchor: فطلب منهم الخفة في مطاوعته أو فاستخف أحلامهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:54-56/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:54-56/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:54-56/r2.claim: They obeyed Pharaoh in what he ordered because they were a wicked people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:54-56/r2.anchor: فيما أمرهم به { إنهم كانوا قوما فسقين } فلذلك أطاعوا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r6.claim: Though thoughtful hearers would see Pharaoh's speech as self-degrading, his followers accepted it because worldly leadership commands the weakly attached, while people resist an unrecognized leader despite great deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r6.anchor: فهم أذل شيء لمن ثبتت له رئاسته دنيوية وإن صار ترابا , وأعصى شيء على من لم تفقه له الناس

BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r7.claim: Pharaoh used deceptive, beguiling speech that diminished his own case to sway people already disposed to foolishness.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r7.anchor: أي بسبب هذه الخدع التي سحرهم بها في هذا الكلام الذي هو في الحقيقة محقر له

BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r8.claim: Their obedience meant acknowledging Pharaoh's kingship and grandeur, affirming his lordship, and rejecting Moses' command.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r8.anchor: بأن أقروا بملكه وأذعنوا لضخامته واعترفوا بربوبيته وردوا أمر موسى

BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r9.claim: Moses had answered every threat and request with signs that surpassed bracelets and angels, so the Egyptians had no reason to obey Pharaoh except affinity in evil character.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r9.anchor: أجابهم إليه , فلم يكن للقبط داع إلى طاعة فرعون بعدما رأوا من الآيات

BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r10.claim: The Egyptians had forceful resolve and pride, except when confronted with the worldly means they were accustomed to obey.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r10.anchor: { قوما } أي عندهم قوة شكائم توجب لهم الشماخة إلا عند من يقهرهم بما يألفون من أسباب الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r11.claim: Their فسق was entrenched departure from God's obedience into disobedience, made a second nature.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r11.anchor: عريقين في الخروج عن طاعة الله إلى معصية , قد صار لهم ذلك خلقا ثانيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r2.claim: Pharaoh's address led his courtiers to obey quickly after his deception swayed them, although they had been ready to follow Moses on seeing the signs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r2.anchor: فتفرع عن نداء فرعون قومه أن أثر بتمويهه في نفوس ملئه فعجلوا بطاعته بعد أن كانوا متهيئين لاتباع موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r3.claim: Lightness is a metaphor for shifting from reflection and hesitation to swift compliance, as an object becomes light after being heavy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r3.anchor: فالخفة مستعارة للانتقال من حالة التأمل في خلع طاعة فرعون والتثاقل في اتباعه إلى التعجيل بالامتثال له كما يخف الشيء بعد التثاقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r4.claim: The phrase also means Pharaoh made them intellectually frivolous: after inwardly crediting Moses because of his signs, they quickly accepted Pharaoh's claims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r4.anchor: والمعنى يرجع إلى أنه استخف عقولهم فأسرعوا إلى التصديق بما قاله بعد أن صدقوا موسى في نفوسهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r5.claim: His people here means only those present at the summons, the elite who were in Pharaoh's company.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r5.anchor: والمراد ب { قومه } هنا بعض القوم ، وهم الذين حضروا مجلس دعوة موسى هؤلاء هم الملأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r6.claim: The added sīn and tāʾ intensify أخف, as in the verse about Satan causing a slip and the Arabic phrase about provoking a sensible person's anger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r6.anchor: والسين والتاء في { استخف } للمبالغة في أخف مثل قوله تعالى : { إنما استزلهم الشيطان }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r7.claim: إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين is grammatically the cause of their obedience; إن is not emphatic because their unbelief was already obvious once Moses called them away from idolatry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r7.anchor: وجملة { إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين } في موضع العلة لجملة { فأطاعوه } كما هو شأن ( إن ) إذا جاءت في غير مقام التأكيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r8.claim: They readily obeyed the chief of unbelief because their unbelief was recent: they had deified Pharaoh, wavered after Moses was sent, then returned to Pharaoh at the slightest pretext.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r8.anchor: لأنهم كانوا يؤلهون فرعون فلما حصل لهم تردد في شأنه ببعثة موسى عليه السلام لم يلبثوا أن رجعوا إلى طاعة فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r9.claim: Fāsiqīn here means unbelievers, as the Qur'an describes these people in the verse about the abode of the wicked.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r9.anchor: والمراد بالفسق هنا : الكفر ، كما قال في شأنهم في آية الأعراف { سأوريكم دار الفاسقين } .

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p322/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p322/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p322/r1.claim: Al-Farraʾ explains istakh affa as “he stirred them up.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p322/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ فاستخف قومه ﴾ قال الفراء استفزهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p322/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p322/r2.speaker: غيره
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p322/r2.claim: Another explanation is that Pharaoh manipulated and deceived them into frivolity of judgment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p322/r2.anchor: وقال غيره استخف أحلامهم وحملهم على خفة الحلم بكيده وغروره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p322/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p322/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p322/r3.claim: They obeyed Pharaoh by rejecting Moses.

MUQATIL:43:54-55/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:54-55/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:54-55/r1.claim: Pharaoh roused and manipulated his people, the Copts, into following him in denial, including his claim in 40:29.

MUQATIL:43:54-55/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:54-55/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:54-55/r2.claim: The Copts obeyed Pharaoh in the denial he urged.
MUQATIL:43:54-55/r2.anchor: { فأطاعوه } في الذي قال لهم على التكذيب

MUQATIL:43:54-55/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:54-55/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:54-55/r3.claim: The people are called transgressors because they were disobedient.
MUQATIL:43:54-55/r3.anchor: { إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين } [آية: 54]، يعني عاصين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p117#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p117#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p117#3/r1.claim: Istakhaffa means he incited his people verbally, led them astray, and made his words effective among them; alternatively, he asked them to be quick and obedient.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p117#3/r1.anchor: استفزهم بالقول واستزلهم وعمل فيهم كلامه وقيل طلب منهم الخفة والطاعة وهي الاسراع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p117#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p117#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p117#3/r2.claim: They obeyed him because they were a people who had left God's religion.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r1.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r1.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī glosses the phrase as Pharaoh making his people foolish; they obeyed because their minds were light and their reason limited.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r1.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: المعنى فاستجهل قومه

QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r2.claim: The verb can mean that joy unsettles someone or that someone induces another to act foolishly; the related verse warns against being unsettled by unbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r2.anchor: يقال: استخفه الفرح أي أزعجه، واستخفه أي حمله على الجهل

QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that Pharaoh provoked his people with speech, and they obeyed him by accepting disbelief.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r3.anchor: وقيل: استفزهم بالقول فأطاعوه على التكذيب

QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r4.claim: A further view says he found them intellectually weak; this alone cannot explain their obedience, so an unstated step must be supplied: he called them to error and they obeyed.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r4.anchor: وقيل: استخف قومه أي وجدهم خفاف العقول. وهذا لا يدل على أنه يجب أن يطيعوه

QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r5.claim: Another view takes the phrase as Pharaoh overpowering his people until they followed him; استخف به means to insult someone.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r5.anchor: وقيل: استخف قومه وقهرهم حتى اتبعوه يقال: استخفه خلاف استثقله

QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r6.claim: They were a people who had departed from obedience to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r6.anchor: { إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين } أي خارجين عن طاعة الله
